title: MediVault AI
subtitle: Patient-controlled health records & digital prescriptions
points: A working prototype using fictional records.
Presented by Mbali Mazibuko · 20 October 2026
notes: Open: Today I will show how one patient can carry her history between doctors, control access, and understand what is recorded. This is a prototype, not a clinical service.

title: The record should travel with the patient
subtitle: Fragmented information interrupts continuity of care.
points: Paper histories and prescriptions can be lost or unavailable.
A new doctor may not have the patient’s previous consultation context.
Patients need both control over sharing and understandable records.
notes: Describe these as the problem we are addressing, not measured research findings. We have not yet quantified time savings or clinical outcomes.

title: One record. Permission before access.
subtitle: A connected patient and doctor workflow.
points: Patient: history, prescriptions, notifications and privacy controls.
Doctor: find a patient, verify identity and request access.
Verified doctor: record a consultation and issue a digital prescription.
notes: Position the solution as patient-controlled. Show that the doctor workflow starts with identity checks and consent rather than browsing everyone’s records.

title: Follow Thandi’s visit
subtitle: A fictional patient, a verified doctor, a visible handover.
points: 01 · Thandi shows her history and patient ID.
02 · Dr Naidoo finds her and obtains access.
03 · The doctor records the visit and reviews a prescription.
04 · Thandi receives it and asks for a plain-language explanation.
notes: Switch to the app. Use the separate demo script for exact clicks. Keep the one-time code out of recordings after the demo. Demonstration data only.

title: Trust must be visible
subtitle: Controls designed into the workflow—not a compliance certification.
points: Patient approval and revocation of doctor access.
Verification gate before clinical writing.
Issued records protected from ordinary patient edits.
Audit trail for key sensitive actions.
notes: These are implemented design controls, not a claim that the system is production-secure or POPIA-certified. Independent security testing and legal assessment are still needed.

title: AI explains. It does not prescribe.
subtitle: An assistant grounded in the patient’s own records.
points: Explain medical terms and summarise recorded history.
Prepare questions for the next doctor visit.
No new diagnosis or dosage changes; emergency guidance directs to urgent help.
notes: Explain that AI can be incomplete or wrong. Show the AI-generated label. If the response indicates demo mode, say it is a fallback, not a live model answer. A clinician remains responsible for care.

title: Prototype today. Clinical readiness next.
subtitle: No real patient data and no dispensing from these prescriptions.
points: Demonstrable now: patient and doctor workflows, access controls, digital records.
Before clinical use: legal/privacy review, security assessment and operational safeguards.
Before prescribing rollout: real HPCSA verification, signatures and pharmacy integration.
notes: Do not claim legal compliance, validated clinical outcomes, or a pharmacy-ready prescription. Production readiness, costs and implementation timeline have not yet been validated.

title: Agree the next validation step
subtitle: Proposed ask: support a scoped discovery and validation phase.
points: Nominate clinical, privacy and operational reviewers.
Define success criteria and test the workflow with fictional cases.
Agree a responsible pilot scope only after the readiness gaps are addressed.
notes: Close: Does this workflow solve a meaningful continuity-of-care problem for your setting? What evidence would you need before supporting a pilot? This is a proposed discussion ask, not a budget or approval already secured.
